questions.e: ُيكت (yaktubu, 'he writes') starts with the present-tense prefix ي and describes an ongoing action, so it is fi'l mudari'. قرأ ,ذهب and ُأكل are past-tense verbs.
The proverb compares time to a sword: if you don't use it well, it cuts you. So time is precious and must be put to good use (استغالله ويجب ثمين الوقت).
In 'knowledge is light', light is a metaphor: knowledge lights up the mind and guides a person to what is right, so it is a means of guidance and understanding, not literal light.
The passage explains 'a friend in need' (الضيق وقت الصديق) as meaning a true friend stays by you in hard times, so a real friend shows himself in difficulty.
The passage says cleanliness is not just a habit but a basic part of faith and piety, so it is part of Islamic conduct, not merely a social custom.
The verse means that when you pursue honour you should not settle for anything below the stars, which is a call for high ambition (العالي الطموح) rather than contentment with little.
ٌصافي ُالسما is a nominal sentence: ُالسما is the subject (مبتدأ) and ٌصافي is the predicate (خبر). Sentences B and C begin with verbs.
A good composition opens with an introduction that defines the topic. So an essay on knowledge should begin with a definition of knowledge and its importance.
زينة العقل means intellect is an adornment: good sense beautifies and improves a person more than outward decoration does.
Learning in childhood is like engraving on stone, meaning what is learnt young stays firm and lasting (ودائم ثابت).
جليس خير الكتاب ('a book is the best companion') means a book is a useful, quiet companion that benefits you without causing harm.
Saying health is dearer than gold means health is a priceless treasure (ثمين كنز), worth more than any wealth.
وجد ّج من ('whoever strives, finds') encourages hard work and perseverance (الجاد العمل) as the way to success.
Describing a school trip means retelling events in order, so the narrative (story-telling) style (القصصي األسلوب) suits it best.
In ٌنشي ُالمعل, the predicate (خبر) ٌنشي is nominative with damma. The other sentences are verbal, with no mubtada' or khabar.
Fasting (الصيام) in Ramadan is itself one of the five pillars of Islam, alongside the testimony of faith, prayer, zakat and Hajj.
قاتل follows the pattern َفا َع, whose masdar is ِفعال or ُمفا َعلة, so its verbal noun is قتال ('fighting'). قتل is the masdar of the simple verb قتل.
Pre-Islamic (Jahili) poetry was known for its strict metre (وزن) and single rhyme (قافية) running through each qasida, and it was rich in rhetoric, not prose.
لن negates the future and puts the present verb in the accusative (َأساف with fatha). So its grammatical effect is nasb, even though its meaning is negation.
Ahmad Shawqi, called الشعراء أمير (Prince of Poets), was born in Cairo, Egypt, in 1868.
هذا ('this', shown here as هذ) is an ism isharah, a demonstrative pronoun used to point to something near. علم and كتب are a noun and a verb, and فوق is an adverb of place.
Hayy ibn Yaqzan, the philosophical tale of a boy who reaches truth through reason alone on an island, was written by the Andalusian thinker Ibn Tufail.
The idiom وساق قدم على (literally 'on foot and leg') means something is going on in full swing, quickly and energetically.
The sentence begins with the verb ُيذاك, followed by its subject ُالطال, so it is a verbal sentence (فعلية جملة). A nominal sentence begins with a noun.
Makkah al-Mukarramah, the holiest city in Islam and home of the Ka'bah, is in the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia.
استغفر adds the letters س ,ا and ت to the root ر ف غ, matching the pattern استفعل, which often means seeking something (here, seeking forgiveness).
The Prophet's migration (Hijrah) from Makkah to Madinah took place in 622 CE, and it marks the start of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar.
ذهب means 'went', خالد is the name, إلى means 'to' and السوق means 'the market', so the sentence is 'Khalid went to the market'.
ُالمجته follows ُالول and agrees with it in case, definiteness and gender, describing it, so it is an adjective (نعت). ٌناج is the predicate.
ُتد ُر comes from the three-letter root درس. The ت at the start is only the present- tense prefix, not an added letter, so the verb is مجرد ثالثي. The correct option is D.
في ('in') is a preposition (جر حرف) that puts the following noun in the genitive, for example فيِ البي.
الهشيم في كالنار ('like fire in dry straw') describes something such as news or a rumour that spreads very quickly (بسرعة تنتشر).
يالذك ُّ follows ُالول and matches it in case, gender and definiteness, describing it, so it is a نعت (adjective). A حال is usually indefinite and accusative.
The Qur'an has 114 surahs, starting with al-Fatihah and ending with an-Nas.
أحب means 'I love' and مدرستي means 'my school' (مدرسة + the possessive ي), so the sentence is 'I love my school'.
ذهب means 'went', أبي means 'my father', and المستشفى إلى means 'to the hospital', which gives 'My father went to the hospital'.
استمع follows the pattern افتعل, whose masdar is افتعال, so the verbal noun is استماع ('listening'). مستمع is the active participle ('listener').
ذلك ('that') points to something far away, so it is a demonstrative pronoun (إشارة اسم), the distant counterpart of هذا.
منزل comes from the root ل ز ن with a prefixed م, matching َم ْف ِعل (shown as مقعل, a misprint), a pattern for nouns of place: the place where one stays.
عين has several meanings (eye, spy, spring). With الماء ('water') and صافية ('clear'), it means a spring (ينبوع).
إذا ,إن and متى can all introduce a conditional sentence, so all the options are conditional words (شرط أدوات).
An essay needs a title, an introduction, a body and a conclusion. A prayer or supplication (الدعاء) is not one of its essential parts.
لم is a particle that negates the past and makes the following present verb jussive (مجزوم), for example ْيذه لم. So it is a particle of negation and jazm.
الفصل إلى ُالتلمي ذهب begins with the verb ذهب, so it is a verbal sentence (فعلية جملة). The other options begin with nouns and are nominal sentences.
The Islamic fast runs from dawn (الفجر) to sunset (المغرب), during which eating, drinking and other things that break the fast are avoided.
طالب commonly takes the broken plural طالب ('students'). طلبة is another accepted plural, while طالبات is the feminine plural.
After ّإ, the subject becomes its noun (ّإ اسم) and takes the accusative (َالصد), while ٌمنجا is its predicate (ّإ خبر).
مستشفى starts with the added letters س ,م and ت before the root ي ف ش, so it follows the pattern ْس َت ْف َعل مُ, used here as a noun of place (a place of healing).
ُالمعل is the one doing the explaining and is nominative, so it is the subject (فاعل). شرح is the verb and الدرس is the object.
سريع means 'fast'. Among the options, عاجل ('quick, hasty') has the same meaning, while بطيء is its opposite and سريح does not mean fast. The correct option is C.
Kitab al-Aghani (The Book of Songs), a huge collection of Arabic songs, poems and poets' biographies, was compiled by Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani in the 10th century.
ّإ is one of the particles of emphasis that put the subject in the accusative (َالل) and the predicate in the nominative (ٌغفو), so it is harf tawkid wa nasb.
قلم (qalam) means 'pen'. Book is كتاب, paper is ورقة and ink is حبر.
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was chosen as the first caliph after the Prophet's death in 632 CE. Umar, Uthman and Ali followed him in that order.
مجتهدة means 'hardworking' (feminine). كسولة means lazy, نشيطة means active or energetic, and جميلة means beautiful.
اإليمان من النظافة is the well-known saying, word for word: النظافة 'cleanliness', من 'part of', اإليمان 'faith'.
Al-Rabita al-Qalamiyya (the Pen League) was founded in New York in 1920 by emigrant (Mahjar) writers such as Gibran Khalil Gibran and Mikhail Naimy.
وسيم ('handsome, good-looking') shares the meaning of جميل ('beautiful'). قصير means short and طويل means tall.
الذي ('who, which') links الطالب to the clause بالجائزة فاز, so it is a relative pronoun (اسم موصول), not a demonstrative or question word.
الفصل means 'the classroom' and في means 'in', so الفصل في ُالطال is the exact translation. البيت is home and المدرسة is school.
A personal letter must carry the writer's address (العنوان) at the top and the signature (التوقيع) at the end, along with the greeting and body.
The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic, as it says itself: مبين عربي بلسان ('in clear Arabic speech').
مكتبة comes from the root ب ت ك with a prefixed م and a final ة, matching the pattern َم ْف َع َلة, which often marks a place (here, a library).
The sound masculine plural adds ون (nominative) or ين to the singular, so معلم becomes أعالم .معلمون is a broken plural of a different word.
The future in Arabic is made with س or سوف plus the present verb, so 'I will travel' is سأسافر and 'tomorrow' is ُسافر .غ ًدا is past and أسافر لن is negative.
In ٌمحم ,َالتفاح ٌمحم َأك does the eating and is nominative, so he is the subject (فاعل). التفاحة is the object (به مفعول).
The first verses (Iqra', Surah al-Alaq) were revealed in the Cave of Hira on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan, as the Qur'an itself says in Surah al-Qadr.
The verb عاد ('he returned') has the masdar عودة ('return'). عيادة means a clinic or visiting the sick, and عادة means habit.
اليوم ('today') tells when something happens, so it is an adverb of time (زمان ظرف). تحت and أمام are adverbs of place.
Risalat al-Ghufran by Abu al-Ala al-Ma'arri is an imaginative epistle describing a journey to heaven and hell. That makes it a fictional letter, not a biography or a scientific essay.
Abu al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, the 10th-century master poet, is known as al-Mutanabbi.
Ali ibn Abi Talib, raised in the Prophet's house, was the first boy to accept Islam. Abu Bakr was the first adult man and Khadijah the first woman.
لن is a particle of negation that makes the present verb accusative (منصوب), so it puts َيفش in nasb.
Adab al-Katib, a classical guide to correct language and style for secretaries and writers, was written by Ibn Qutaybah.
يقرأون means 'they read / are reading' and القرآن is 'the Qur'an'. يدرسون means study, يص ّلون means pray and يكتبون means write.
ّالج means 'the weather', بارد means 'cold' and اليوم means 'today'. حار means hot and مشمس means sunny.
Mahjar (émigré) writers in the Americas often expressed longing for their homeland (إلى الحنين الوطن), along with deep feeling and reflection.
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, the just Umayyad ruler, is often called the fifth rightly guided caliph because his rule followed the example of the first four.
ذكية means 'smart' and مهذبة means 'polite, well-mannered', so ومهذبة ذكية الفتاة matches the sentence.
Taha Husayn's works, such as al-Ayyam, deal frankly with real social life, education and hardship in Egypt, which is why he is placed with the realist school.
